### Q0SAA3 — Lysylphosphatidylglycerol biosynthesis bifunctional protein LysX
- Organism: Rhodococcus jostii (strain RHA1)
- Reviewed: True
- Source: local_uniprot_swissprot_xml
- Homology: identity=47.9%, query coverage=91.8%, target coverage=63.0%, E-value=7.71e-203
- function: Catalyzes the production of L-lysyl-tRNA(Lys)transfer and the transfer of a lysyl group from L-lysyl-tRNA(Lys) to membrane-bound phosphatidylglycerol (PG), which produces lysylphosphatidylglycerol (LPG), one of the components of the bacterial membrane with a positive net charge. LPG synthesis contributes to the resistance to cationic antimicrobial peptides (CAMPs) and likely protects M.tuberculosis against the CAMPs produced by competiting microorganisms (bacteriocins). In fact, the modification of anionic phosphatidylglycerol with positively charged L-lysine results in repulsion of the peptides (By similarity).

entities.name: LysX

Curated homologs are multi-pass membrane proteins and bind three Mg2+ ions per subunit.

entities.name: Lysyl-tRNA formation
observations: L-lysine + ATP + tRNA(Lys) → lysyl-tRNA(Lys) + AMP + diphosphate.
This is the aminoacylation reaction catalyzed by lysine--tRNA ligase activity, EC 6.1.1.6; Mg2+ is required in curated homologs.
Rhea references reported by the protein analysis include RHEA:20792, RHEA:9696, and RHEA:9697.

entities.name: Lysyl-PG formation
observations: The transferred lysyl group modifies membrane phosphatidylglycerol, producing a more positively charged lipid; curated homologs associate this activity with EC 2.3.2.3.
Rhea reference reported by the protein analysis: RHEA:10668.

entities.name: LysX membrane topology
observations: The sequence contains a strongly hydrophobic N-terminal segment consistent with multiple transmembrane helices, while most of the C-terminal half is soluble and highly charged.
This architecture agrees with a membrane-associated phosphatidylglycerol lysyltransferase coupled to a cytosolic lysyl-tRNA synthetase domain.
